title: Orchestrated fallthrough and thresholded traffic curation for hosted API regional rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Hardening the hosted API regional rollout pipeline by introducing a configurable fallthrough routing layer and per-region thresholded traffic curation. Current problems: sudden region-level latency spikes and downstream overloads during cutovers cause global tail latency regressions and customer errors. This ticket implements a traffic curation controller that applies throttles, soft-deny fallthroughs to compatible model variants or lower-cost capacity tiers, and automated SLO-aware holdpoints that can pause a rollout and trigger mitigation playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: New traffic curation controller deployed to staging and prod can limit ingress to a region based on configurable token-bucket thresholds and error-rate thresholds

When region-level P99 latency exceeds threshold X or error-rate exceeds Y for >=2 minutes, the controller automatically shifts a configurable percent of new sessions to fallthrough variants with no manual intervention
Rollouts respect holdpoint gates: canary -> ramp -> full, with automatic rollback if SLO regressions exceed configured tolerances
Observability: per-region dashboards show pre/post curation throughput, fallthrough rate, and recovered latency within 5 minutes of action
Playbook runbook added with clear steps for manual abort, forced rollback, and forensics links
design_decisions: Implement controller as a control-plane microservice that publishes routing policies to edge proxies (Envoy) via xDS; avoids changing runtime request path
Use token-bucket for short-term surge protection and an exponentially-weighted error-rate window for sustained failures
Fallthrough destinations are prioritized: first-compatible model variant (quantized/cheaper), then cross-region routing to healthy region, then 503 with backoff headers if no safe fallback
SLO gate thresholds are configurable per-customer tier and per-model; defaults set conservatively for LTS channel traffic
Instrument decisions with immutable action-IDs surfaced in logs so rollbacks and action attributions are auditable
implementation_steps: Schema: define routing-policy CRD covering token buckets, error windows, and fallthrough targets
Controller: implement policy evaluation loop with simulation mode (no-op) behind feature flag
Proxy integration: add xDS resources and staging Envoy filters that accept policy metadata
Telemetry: emit action events, pre/post metrics (latency distribution, error-rate, fallthrough-count) to Console and Datadog
Canary: deploy to single region with synthetic workload; run chaos tests (delay injection, spike load)
Rollout: staged multi-region rollout with 0->25->50->100 ramps, SLO gates between stages
Rollback automation: if gate fails, controller immediately reverts to previous routing policy and triggers alerting and runbook links
